momentum.note: I lack the prior price series needed to confirm any upward moves, so I cannot identify clear momentum today. I will keep the book in cash to earn the 4.11% Treasury bill rate.

value.note: Cash sits idle earning the Treasury bill rate, and no instrument is clearly cheaper than its recent history. I continue to monitor EMB and HYG for deeper discounts before committing more capital.

macro.note: With the Fed likely to keep rates elevated and oil showing limited upside, I’m scaling back cyclical exposure and adding inflation‑protected bonds. Cash will sit at the Treasury bill rate until the next FOMC.

careful.note: The upcoming 2026‑12‑08 FOMC meeting is the next catalyst; until its outcome we see no instrument offering a yield above the 4.11% cash rate, so we keep the book fully in cash to preserve capital. This maintains the anchor position and avoids unnecessary risk while we await clearer direction.

contrarian.note: The desk's consensus remains centered on bond funds, expecting a dovish Fed, which leaves me skeptical of continued fixed‑income demand. I view silver as a contrarian play that should benefit if bond sentiment wanes and inflation concerns re‑emerge, so I’m adding a modest position.

fx.note: I am keeping the bulk of the book in cash ahead of the Dec 8 FOMC, letting the Treasury sweep earn the 4.11% rate. I will watch EURUSD and other pairs for any USD weakness after the meeting before taking new positions.

metals.note: The gold position is down 12% from its cost, and silver is essentially gone, leaving the combined metal exposure just under 15% of the book. I’m keeping the allocation low to stay clear of the 5% drop rule, but I’m watching for a potential reversal if the Fed’s December meeting signals tighter policy. For now, cash sits at the Treasury rate and I’m ready to act if metals drift further.

index.note: All three core holdings sit just under the 25% cap, with TLT at 24.5% – exactly 0.5% under the target, which does not trigger a rebalance. Cash sits at 26.2% of NAV, comfortably below the 27% ceiling. Given the modest declines and no material drift, I will hold.
